arxiv-2106-05926.title: Scalar Curvature Invariants in Classical and Quantum Gravity
arxiv-2106-05926.creator: B. Shakerin a,b, D.D. McNutt c, B. Mattingly a,b, A. Kar a,b, W. Julius a,b, M. Gorban a,b, C. Watson a,b, P. Brown a,b, J. S. Lee a,b, E. W. Davis b, G. B. Cleaver a,b
arxiv-2106-05926.description: Abstract A short review of scalar curvature invariants in gravity theories is presented. We introduce how these invariants are constructed and discuss the minimal number of invariants required for a given spacetime. We then discuss applications of these invariants and focus on three topics that are of particular interest in modern gravity theories.

arxiv-2305-04168.title: EFX Allocations for Indivisible Chores: Matching-Based Approach
arxiv-2305-04168.creator: Yusuke Kobayashi, Ryoga Mahara, Souta Sakamoto
arxiv-2305-04168.description: Abstract One of the most important topics in discrete fair division is whether an EFX allocation exists for any instance. Although the existence of EFX allocations is a standing open problem for both goods and chores, the understanding of the existence of EFX allocations for chores is less established compared to goods.

arxiv-2312-14208.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by . We suggest a new explanation of flatness of galaxies rotation curves without invoking dark matter. For this purpose a new gravitational tensor field is introduced in addition to the metric tensor. arxiv-2403-12126.title: Non-Abelian and Abelian descendants of vortex spin liquid: fractional quantum spin Hall effect in twisted MoTe 2
arxiv-2403-12126.creator: Ya-Hui Zhang
arxiv-2403-12126.description: Abstract The recent experimental observation of a potential fractional quantum spin Hall (FQSH) state in the twisted MoTe 2 system has sparked theoretical explorations at total filling ν T = 1 \nu_{T}=1 of a pair of C = ± 1 C=\pm 1 Chern bands from the two spins (locked to valley).

arxiv-2501-08229.title: Enhancing Train Transportation in Sri Lanka: A Smart IOT based Multi-Subsystem Approach using MQTT Thanks: dhanushkasandeepa@gmail.com, narmada.g@sliit.lk, jaliya.wijayaraja@gmail.com (Correspondence author: Dhanushka Balasingham)
arxiv-2501-08229.creator: Dhanushka Balasingham, Sadeesha Samarathunga, Anuththara Bandara, Gayantha Godakanda Arachchige, Narmada Gamage, Jaliya L. Wijayaraja
arxiv-2501-08229.description: Abstract This research proposes a system as a solution for the challenges faced by Sri Lanka’s historic railway system, such as scheduling delays, overcrowding, manual ticketing, and management inefficiencies. It proposes a multi-subsystem approach, incorporating GPS tracking, RFID-based e-ticketing, seat reservation, and vision-based people counting.

arxiv-2504-06477.title: Sparsified-Learning for High-Dimensional Heavy-Tailed Locally Stationary Time Series, Concentration and Oracle Inequalities
arxiv-2504-06477.creator: Yingjie Wang wyj202007@nuaa.edu.cn, Mokhtar Z. Alaya alayaelm@utc.fr, Salim Bouzebda salim.bouzebda@utc.fr, Xinsheng Liu xsliu@nuaa.edu.cn
arxiv-2504-06477.description: Abstract Sparse learning is ubiquitous in many machine learning tasks. It aims to regularize the goodness-of-fit objective by adding a penalty term to encode structural constraints on the model parameters. In this paper, we develop a flexible sparse learning framework tailored to high-dimensional heavy-tailed locally stationary time series (LSTS).

arxiv-2512-01495.title: ELVIS: Enhance Low-light for Video Instance Segmentation in the Dark
arxiv-2512-01495.creator: Joanne Lin, Ruirui Lin, Yini Li, David Bull, Nantheera Anantrasirichai
arxiv-2512-01495.description: Abstract Video instance segmentation (VIS) for low-light content remains highly challenging for both humans and machines alike, due to adverse imaging conditions including noise, blur and low-contrast. The lack of large-scale annotated datasets and the limitations of current synthetic pipelines, particularly in modeling temporal degradations, further hinder progress.

pmc-12679342.title: Synergy Effects in a Bimetallic Ru ─ Pt Alloy Catalyst for Low‐H2‐Pressure Hydrogenolysis of Low‐Density Polyethylene
pmc-12679342.creator: Yukari Yamazaki, Xiongjie Jin, Weihan Sun, Satoshi Yamamoto, Katsutoshi Nomoto, Kohei Takahashi, Hiroki Miura, Tetsuya Shishido, Akira Nakayama, Kyoko Nozaki
pmc-12679342.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Hydrogenolysis of low‐density polyethylene (LDPE) under low pressure of H2 has been accomplished with a Ru─Pt bimetallic alloy catalyst. Using Ru5Pt1/CeO2 (atomic ratio of Ru to Pt is 5:1) as a catalyst, LDPE was efficiently converted (97.6 ± 2.5% conversion) to gas and liquid hydrocarbons under 5 bar of H2 at 200 °C, whereas Ru/CeO2 and Pt/CeO2 showed much lower conversion (45.7 ± 3.7% and < 1%, respectively), under the same conditions.
